items.title: Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1): groupoids, $\mathrm{mor}(x, y)$ and the orbit space $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226)
book.statement:
A *groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is a small category consisting of the set $X$ of objects, denoted by $x$, and the set $\mathbf X$ of morphisms (arrows), which are assumed to be invertible, and the following five structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$. (1) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ assign to every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X$ its source $s(\varphi) = x$ and its target $t(\varphi) = y$. (2) The associative multiplication (composition) map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $m(\varphi, \psi) = \varphi \circ \psi$, is defined on the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X = \{(\varphi, \psi) \in \mathbf X \times \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) = t(\psi)\}$, so that if $\psi : x \to z$ and $\varphi : z \to y$, then $\varphi \circ \psi : x \to y$. (3) For every object $x \in X$ there exists the unit morphism $1_x : x \to x$ in $\mathbf X$, a 2-sided unit for the composition: $\varphi \circ 1_x = \varphi$ and $1_x \circ \psi = \psi$ for all $\varphi, \psi \in \mathbf X$ satisfying $s(\varphi) = x = t(\psi)$; these define the unit map $u : X \to \mathbf X$, $u(x) = 1_x$. (4) For every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there exists the inverse morphism $\varphi^{-1} : y \to x$, a 2-sided inverse: $\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_y$ and $\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_x$; these define the inverse map $\iota : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $\iota(\varphi) = \varphi^{-1}$.

After the definition: $\mathrm{mor}(x, y) \subset \mathbf X$ is the set of all morphisms $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = x$ and $t(\varphi) = y$. The *orbit space* $|X| = X/\sim$ is the quotient of the set of objects by the equivalence relation $x \sim y$ if and only if there exists a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; the class of $x$ is $|x| := \{y \in X \mid y \sim x\}$, and $\pi : X \to |X|$, $\pi(x) = |x|$, is the quotient map.

lean.statement: `GroupoidStr Obj Mor`: types of objects and morphisms with the maps `src`, `tgt`, `comp`, `unit`, `inv` and the laws `src_comp`, `tgt_comp`, `comp_assoc` on composable pairs $s(\varphi) = t(\psi)$, `src_unit`, `tgt_unit`, `comp_unit` ($\varphi \circ 1_{s(\varphi)} = \varphi$), `unit_comp` ($1_{t(\varphi)} \circ \varphi = \varphi$), `src_inv`, `tgt_inv`, `comp_inv` ($\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_{t(\varphi)}$), `inv_comp` ($\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_{s(\varphi)}$) (fields of the structure). `mor x y` and `morOn A` (the morphisms with source and target in $A$) are sets of morphisms; `Isomorphic x y` is the existence of $\varphi : x \to y$, `orbitSetoid` the equivalence relation, `OrbitSpace` $= |X|$ its quotient and `π` the projection, with $\pi(x) = \pi(y) \iff x \sim y$ (`π_eq_π_iff`). `saturation A` $= \pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$, `IsSaturated A`, equivalent to: $s(\varphi) \in A \Rightarrow t(\varphi) \in A$ (`isSaturated_iff`). `Ob`, `instGroupoid`: the same data as a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Groupoid`, whose isomorphism relation is `orbitSetoid` (`orbitSetoid_eq`).

items.title: Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2): the isotropy group $G_x$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 288 (2017 p. 226)
book.statement: For fixed $x \in X$ we denote by $G_x$ the isotropy group (stabilizer group) of $x$, defined by $G_x = \{\varphi \in \mathbf X \mid \varphi : x \to x\}$.

items.title: Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3): ep-groupoids

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227)
book.statement: An *ep-groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ consists of a groupoid equipped with M-polyfold structures on the object set $X$ and the morphism set $\mathbf X$ having the following properties. (1) (étale) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms. (2) The unit map $u$ and the inverse map $\iota$ are sc-smooth. (3) (Properness) Every point $x \in X$ possesses an open neighborhood $V(x)$ of $x$ in $X$ such that the map $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper. Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is in a natural way an M-polyfold in view of Lemma 2.8 in [38], and we require (4) the multiplication map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$ is sc-smooth. In particular, all the structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$ are sc-smooth maps.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid Obj Mor` extends `GroupoidStr` by M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor` on the Hausdorff paracompact spaces $X$, $\mathbf X$ and the conditions (1) `isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`; (2) `isScSmoothMap_unit`, `isScSmoothMap_inv`; (3) `exists_isProperMap`: every $x$ has an open $V \ni x$ such that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V) \to X$ is a proper map (Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction); (4) `isScSmoothComp`, i.e. `IsScSmoothComp`: $m$ is sc-smooth on $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ with the sub-M-polyfold structure of Part I (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`). (4) is equivalent to the sheet form `IsScSmoothCompSheet`: for every sheet $\sigma$ of $s$ over $V$, $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t(\psi)), \psi)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$ (`isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`); $s$ and $t$ are sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_src`, `isScSmoothMap_tgt`).

diff: As for every M-polyfold of the project (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are Hausdorff and paracompact (a standing hypothesis).

(3) is existential per point. The universal form "for every open $V \ni x$" does not hold for the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$, while every smaller open neighbourhood of a good one works (V7.4, V7.59) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 3, 103).

"Lemma 2.8 in [38]" cites the paper *A General Fredholm Theory III*, an external reference, not a misprint; its statement in the book is Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15; preprint 2.46), which the formalization uses. The proofs use the equivalent sheet form of (4) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 4).

items.title: Properness and its sequential form

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227; used on pp. 292–346 (2017 pp. 230–254)
book.statement: Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) asks that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ be proper. The proofs use this in the form: if $s(\varphi_k) \in \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ and $t(\varphi_k)$ converges in $X$, then, "after perhaps taking a subsequence", $(\varphi_k)$ converges in $\mathbf X$ (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 230; Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230); Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), p. 307 (2017 p. 238); Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), 2017 p. 248; Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), 2017 p. 254), or through the compactness of preimages of compact sets (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), p. 342 (2017 p. 251)). After Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) (p. 289 (2017 p. 227)) the text points out that this properness differs from that of classical Lie groupoids, which requires $(s, t) : \mathbf X \to X \times X$ to be proper, a requirement too weak for some of the constructions.

lean.statement: For $t$ restricted to $s^{-1}(Q)$, between metrizable spaces: Mathlib's properness is equivalent to the sequential criterion (`isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`, `exists_tendsto_subseq_of_isProperMap`, `isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`, `isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed`; for M-polyfolds `MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`) and to the compactness of preimages of compact sets (`MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage`). Properness passes from $\mathrm{cl}\,V$ to $\mathrm{cl}\,V'$ for $V' \subseteq V$ (`isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono`); a proper restriction has closed images $t(s^{-1}(Q'))$ for $Q' \subseteq Q$ with $s^{-1}(Q')$ closed (`isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`), forces $Q$ to be closed in the presence of units (`isClosed_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`), and has finite fibres when $t$ is locally injective (`finite_setOf_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`).

diff: The text uses the equivalence without comment; it holds because M-polyfolds are metrizable (Part I, Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2), the preprint's Theorem 2.16) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 3).
The comparison with the classical properness of $(s, t)$ has no formal content and is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 7, item 113).

items.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
book.statement: Since $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of an ep-groupoid has an extension to a local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ satisfying $\hat\varphi(x) = y$, defined as follows: there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi) \subset \mathbf X$ and $U(x), U(y) \subset X$ such that $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to U(y)$. In the case that $\varphi$ is smooth, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; more generally $T\hat\varphi : TU(s(\varphi)) \to TU(t(\varphi))$. $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$; only in the case that $\varphi$ is smooth is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): associated to a smooth morphism $\varphi$ we have the so-called associated local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, as well as its tangent $T\varphi$.

lean.statement: `Sheet`: an open set `carrier` $= \mathbf U(\varphi)$ of morphisms with sc-diffeomorphisms $s : \mathbf U \to U(x)$ (`srcSet`) and $t : \mathbf U \to U(y)$ (`tgtSet`) and their inverses; every morphism lies in one (`exists_sheet`, `sheetAt`, `mem_sheetAt`). `Sheet.hat` $= t \circ (s|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $U(x) \to U(y)$ with inverse $s \circ (t|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ (`Sheet.isScDiffeoOn_hat`); for a morphism, `hat φ` is that of `sheetAt φ`, an sc-diffeomorphism (`isScDiffeoOn_hat`) with $\hat\varphi(s(\varphi)) = t(\varphi)$ (`hat_src`). `tangentMor φ` defines $T\varphi$ on the tangent space of $X$ through a tangent vector of $\mathbf X$ at $\varphi$; no property of it is proved.

items.title: The levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228)
book.statement: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are equipped with the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset X_2 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} X_k$ and similarly for $\mathbf X$; $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_k$. For $x$ in the M-polyfold $X$, $ml(x) \in \mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$ is the largest non-negative integer $m$, or $\infty$, such that $x \in X_m$. Since the source and target maps are local sc-diffeomorphisms and therefore preserve the levels, $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; consequently the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0}|X_k|$ of the orbit space. The degeneracy indices $d_X : X \to \mathbb N$ and $d_{\mathbf X} : \mathbf X \to \mathbb N$ are invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7)), so $d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$; in particular $d_X(x) = d_X(x')$ if $x \sim x'$.

lean.statement: `mem_levelSet_src_iff`, `mem_levelSet_tgt_iff`: $s(\varphi) \in X_m \iff \varphi \in \mathbf X_m \iff t(\varphi) \in X_m$. `MPolyfold.maxLevel` is $ml$, preserved by local sc-diffeomorphisms (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq`), as is the degeneracy index (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq`), so $d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ (`degIndex_src`, `degIndex_tgt`). `orbitLevel k` $= \pi(X_k) = |X_k|$.

diff: The set $|X_\infty|$ and the identity $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$ are not stated (gap G.72); they are immediate, as $ml$ is constant on classes. The density of $X_\infty$ in every $X_k$, which the text states without proof, is not formalized; Part I proves it only for sc-Banach spaces, not for M-polyfolds (gap G.73) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 112, 116).
Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7) is the preprint's Proposition 2.24.

items.title: Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6): tame ep-groupoids; $\mathbf X$ is then tame

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 228
book.statement: The ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is called *tame* if the object space $X$ is a tame M-polyfold as introduced in Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19). In a tame ep-groupoid not only $X$ is a tame M-polyfold but also $\mathbf X$ is a tame M-polyfold. This follows from the facts that $\mathbf X$ is locally sc-diffeomorphic by $s$ to $X$ and the tameness condition is invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.IsTame` is `MPolyfold.IsTame` of the object M-polyfold: an equivalent atlas of charts modelled on tame retracts exists (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)). A chart is transported along an sc-diffeomorphism to a tame chart (`MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart`), so the domain of a local sc-diffeomorphism into a tame M-polyfold is tame (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`), and for surjective ones the domain is tame iff the target is (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective`); applied to $s$, this is the tameness of $\mathbf X$.

diff: "Tame" is read as the existence of an equivalent tame atlas; read as "every chart is modelled on a tame retract" the definition would be unsatisfiable. It is satisfiable (`isTame_trivial_rn`, `Examples.isTame_reflection`) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 7, 106).
Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19) is the preprint's Definition 2.37.

items.title: Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): the category $\mathcal{EP}$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), p. 290 (2017 p. 228)
book.statement: By $\mathcal{EP}$ we denote the category whose objects are the ep-groupoids and whose morphisms $f : (X, \mathbf X) \to (Y, \mathbf Y)$ are the functors which are sc-smooth maps between the object spaces as well as the morphism spaces.

lean.statement: `GroupoidFunctor`: maps `obj`, `mor` commuting with $s$, $t$, with $m$ on composable pairs, and with $u$; the compatibility with $\iota$ is derived (`GroupoidFunctor.mor_inv`); identities and composites (`GroupoidFunctor.id`, `GroupoidFunctor.comp`), the Mathlib functor (`GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor`) and the induced map of orbit spaces (`GroupoidFunctor.orbitMap`). `EpFunctor X Y`: a functor that is sc-smooth on objects and on morphisms (fields `isScSmoothMap_obj`, `isScSmoothMap_mor`); `EpFunctor.id`, `EpFunctor.comp`, `EpFunctor.ext`; `EP` is the type of ep-groupoids, a category with the ep-functors as morphisms.

items.title: The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): sc-smoothness on objects suffices

book.label: §7.1, after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), pp. 290 ff. (2017 pp. 228–229)
book.statement: It is sufficient to require that the functor $f$ is sc-smooth between the object spaces $X \to Y$, because the sc-smoothness of $f : \mathbf X \to \mathbf Y$ follows from the properties of the source map $s : \mathbf X \to X$: given $\varphi \in \mathbf X$ and $f(\varphi) = \psi \in \mathbf Y$ there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi)$, $\mathbf U(\psi)$, $U(s(\varphi))$ and $U(s(\psi))$ satisfying $f(U(s(\varphi))) \subset U(s(\psi))$ and $f(\mathbf U(\varphi)) \subset \mathbf U(\psi)$; moreover, $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(s(\varphi))$ and $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms. Therefore the claim follows from the formula $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ for all $\gamma \in \mathbf U(\varphi)$.

lean.statement: `mor_eq_srcInv_obj_src`: if $f(\gamma)$ lies in a sheet of $s$ with inverse $\sigma$, then $f(\gamma) = \sigma(f(s(\gamma)))$. `isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous`: a functor that is sc-smooth on objects and **continuous on morphisms** is sc-smooth on morphisms; `isScSmoothMap_mor_iff_continuous`: for a functor sc-smooth on objects, sc-smoothness on morphisms is equivalent to continuity there; `EpFunctor.continuous_mor`, `EpFunctor.ofContinuous`. `Examples.remark_definition_7_7_counterexample`: on the ep-groupoid of $\mathbb Z/3$ acting trivially on $\mathbb R$ there is a functor, sc-smooth on objects, that is neither continuous nor sc-smooth on morphisms and is no ep-functor.

diff: **Does not hold as we read it.** The neighbourhoods with $f(\mathbf U(\varphi)) \subset \mathbf U(\psi)$ need $f$ to be continuous on morphisms. On the ep-groupoid of $\mathbb Z/3$ acting trivially on $\mathbb R$, the functor that is the identity on objects and maps $(g, y)$ to $(g, y)$ for $y \le 0$ and to $(g^2, y)$ for $y > 0$ is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on morphisms (Findings, Chapter 7, items 9, 104).
For functors continuous on morphisms the text's argument goes through, and needs only a sheet $\mathbf U(\psi)$ of $s$ at $\psi = f(\varphi)$ and $\mathbf U(\varphi) = f^{-1}(\mathbf U(\psi))$.

items.title: The quotient topology of $|X|$ and Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1): $\pi$ is open

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 229
book.statement: The orbit space $|X|$ is equipped with the quotient topology, the finest topology for which the projection $\pi : X \to |X|$, $x \mapsto |x|$, is continuous: a subset $V$ of $|X|$ is open if and only if $\pi^{-1}(V)$ is open in $X$. Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) (Openness of $\pi$): Let $(X, \mathbf X)$ be an ep-groupoid and assume that the orbit space $|X|$ is equipped with the quotient topology. Then the projection map $\pi : X \to |X|$ is open.

items.title: Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3): the local closure relation

items.title: Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10): invariant sc-smooth majorants

book.label: §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10), p. 346 (2017 p. 255)
book.statement: We assume that $X$ is an ep-groupoid with a paracompact orbit space $|X|$ and the object M-polyfold $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity. Suppose further that $x \in X$ and $U(x)$ and $V(x)$ are open neighborhoods of $x$ satisfying $U(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(U(x)) \subset V(x)$ and such that $V(x)$ admits the natural $G_x$-action and $U(x)$ is invariant. If $\beta : X \to [0, 1]$ is a continuous function with support in $U(x)$ and invariant under the $G_x$-action on $V(x)$, then there exists an sc-smooth function $f : X \to [0, \infty)$ with support in $V(x)$, which is, in addition, invariant under the $G_x$-action on $V(x)$ and satisfies $\beta(y) \le f(y)$ for all $y \in X$.

lean.statement: `lemma_7_10`: let $|X|$ be paracompact (kept, not used) and let the object M-polyfold admit sc-smooth partitions of unity; let $R$ be a natural representation at $x$, its $U$ playing $V(x)$, and $U$ open with $\mathrm{cl}\,U \subseteq V(x)$ and $G_x$-invariant; let $\beta : X \to [0, 1]$ be continuous (kept, not used) with $\mathrm{supp}\,\beta \subseteq U$ and $\beta(g \ast y) = \beta(y)$ on $V(x)$. Then there is an sc-smooth $f \ge 0$ with $\mathrm{supp}\,f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}\,U$ and $\mathrm{supp}\,f \subseteq V(x)$, invariant on $V(x)$, with $\beta \le f$.

diff: The conclusion adds $\mathrm{supp}\,f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_X(U(x))$, which the proof gives and the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) needs; the hypothesis $x \in U(x)$ is not used and is omitted (Findings, Chapter 7, item 93).
The partition of unity "of $V(x)$" is taken for a cover of $X$, since the hypothesis is that $X$, not $V(x)$, admits sc-smooth partitions of unity.

items.title: The proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

book.label: §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)
book.statement: Consider the open covering $(|U_\lambda|)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of $|X|$. For every $x \in X$ take an open neighborhood $V(x)$ with: (1) there exists an open neighborhood $W(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action such that $V(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subset W(x)$ and $V(x)$ is invariant; (2) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper; (3) there exists a $\lambda$ with $V(x) \subset U_\lambda$; (4) $(\pi^{-1}(|V(x)|) \setminus V(x)) \cap W(x) = \emptyset$. Take a locally finite refinement $(V'_i)_{i \in I}$ of $(|V(x)|)_{x \in X}$, with $V'_i \subset |V(x_i)|$, open $V''_i$ with $V''_i \subset \mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(V''_i) \subset V'_i$ and $|X| = \bigcup_i V''_i$; $U''_i = V(x_i) \cap \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$ is invariant under the $G_{x_i}$-action, with saturation $U_i = \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$. Take a continuous partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ subordinate to $(V''_i)$; $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ has support in $U''_i \subset V(x_i)$. Using the sc-smooth partitions of unity of $X$, approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ by Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) by an sc-smooth $f_i$ supported in $V(x_i)$ with $f_i \ge (\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$; average using the $G_{x_i}$-action, extend to the saturation of $V(x_i)$ and then by $0$ outside, which gives a function $h_i$ compatible with morphisms. The sum $h$ of all $h_i$ is locally finite and always bigger than $0$, and $(h_i/h)$ is the desired partition of unity for the ep-groupoid $X$.

lean.statement: `exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen`: inside every open $W \ni x$ there are a natural representation and an open invariant $V \ni x$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,V \subseteq U \subseteq W$ and $\mathrm{cl}\,V$ proper ((1)–(3)); (4) follows: an object of $U$ isomorphic to one of $V$ lies in $V$ (`mem_of_π_mem_image_of_invariant`, `saturation_diff_inter_eq_empty`). `orbitExtension`: the extension of an invariant function on $U$ to the saturation and by $0$, sc-smooth when its support is proper and inside $U$ (`isScSmoothMap_orbitExtension`). `exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn`: for disjoint closed $s, t \subseteq |X|$ there is a continuous $F : |X| \to [0, 1]$, $0$ on $s$ and $1$ on $t$, with $F \circ \pi$ sc-smooth. `admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx`: Part I's normalization through Mathlib's bump coverings. `theorem_7_4` assembles these.

diff: (4) is not a further choice: it follows from (1). Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) is applied with $W(x_i)$ in the role of $V(x)$ and $U''_i$ in that of $U(x)$, where the text reads $V(x_i)$ in the role of $V(x)$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 94).

"The sum of all $h_i$ is locally finite" needs $\mathrm{supp}\,f_i \subseteq \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V'_i)$, the support bound of V7.66; the sc-smoothness of $h_i$ uses that saturations of proper sets are closed (V7.61).

The normalization $(h_i/h)$ and the return from the index set of the refinement to $\Lambda$, which the text leaves implicit, are replaced by Mathlib's bump coverings, as in Part I's Theorem 5.5.10 (2017: 5.12; preprint 5.37), with the text's construction as the Urysohn input.
In (2) the extracted text has "$t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \to X$", a closing parenthesis missing (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 96).

items.title: Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3): sc-Hilbert atlases

book.label: §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3), p. 347 (2017 p. 256)
book.statement: Let $X$ be an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space $|X|$. We assume that the object M-polyfold admits an atlas consisting of charts whose local models $(O, C, E)$ have the property that the $E_0$ are Hilbert spaces. Then every open covering of $X$ by saturated open subsets $(U_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ possesses a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity of the ep-groupoid $X$. (The proof: the assumption on the atlas implies that the object M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, by Appendix 5.5, Proposition 5.5.8 (2017: 5.6), Theorem 5.5.10 (2017: 5.12) and Corollary 5.5.17 (2017: 5.2); then Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) applies.)

lean.statement: `corollary_7_3`: if $|X|$ is paracompact and every $x$ lies in a chart of the object M-polyfold whose $E_0$ is a Hilbert space ($\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)$ for a continuous bilinear $b$) and **satisfies** `GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement` (Part I's Theorem 5.5.16 (2017: 5.14) for $E_0$ and $k = \infty$), then $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity. `MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert`: the step of Part I. `corollary_7_3_hypotheses_rn`: the hypotheses hold for the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^1$.

chips: Hilbert atlas: one chart per point
diff: The theorem of Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler (Part I's Theorem 5.5.16 (2017: 5.14), the preprint's Theorem 5.43) is an explicit hypothesis, as in Part I (gap G.53); it holds for finite-dimensional spaces (`godefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement_of_finiteDimensional`) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 95, 114).

"An atlas consisting of charts whose local models have Hilbert spaces $E_0$" is existential, one chart per point; "every compatible chart" would be unsatisfiable (Findings, Chapter 7, item 106). Proposition 5.5.8, Theorem 5.5.10 and Corollary 5.5.17 (2017: Proposition 5.6, Theorem 5.12 and Corollary 5.2) are the preprint's Proposition 5.35, Theorem 5.37 and Corollary 5.44.

notFormalized.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the tangent $T\varphi$ as an sc-isomorphism
notFormalized.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: For a smooth morphism $\varphi$, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$, and only for smooth $\varphi$ is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) associates with a smooth morphism $\varphi$ the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and its tangent $T\varphi$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond the definition: `tangentMor` defines $T\varphi$ (V7.5), but that it is well defined, equal to $T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$, bijective, a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and an sc-operator for smooth $\varphi$ is not formalized; the linearity needs the linear structure of the tangent spaces, which the project does not have (gap G.7). Not used in Chapter 7; deferred to Chapter 8 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110). Since 2026-11-07 (Chapter 8): well defined, $T\varphi(Ts(h)) = Tt(h)$ for every $h \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ (`tangentMor_tSrc`), and functorial, $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMor_comp`), with the description of $T\mathbf X$ by the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ of Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (`remark_8_1`); the bijectivity and linearity of $T\varphi$, $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$ and the sc-operator property remain not formalized (V8.12; Findings, Chapter 8, item 112).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017; rewritten in 2021 as Theorem 7.2.14): $\mathbf X^R$ Hausdorff and paracompact
notFormalized.label: §7.2, Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), pp. 313–324 (2017 pp. 242–244)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9): the reduced morphism set $\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure. Proposition 7.10 (2017): every ep-groupoid $X$ possesses an associated reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, and $X_R$ is effective. Since an M-polyfold is a paracompact Hausdorff space (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), these assert in particular that $\mathbf X^R$, with the quotient topology, is Hausdorff and paracompact, for every ep-groupoid $X$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for a general ep-groupoid: as we read it, the proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) gives neither property, and both are hypotheses (`[T2Space X.ReducedMor] [ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor]`) of `reducedPolyfold` and so of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017) (V7.39, V7.40). They are discharged for effective $X$, and so for the trivial ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold, and paracompactness follows from regularity when $\mathbf X$ is second countable. Hausdorffness fails in general: for $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff (`Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`, formalized after the round-trip audit). Not formalized: whether $\mathbf X^R$ is paracompact when it is Hausdorff, and whether Hausdorffness with $\mathbf X$ second countable suffices for paracompactness (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 60, 107, 111).

notFormalized.title: The filtration of $|X|$: the set $|X_\infty|$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 228
notFormalized.book: Since $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$, the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} |X_k|$ of the orbit space $|X| = X/\sim$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond the levels: $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$ is `orbitLevel k`, and $s$, $t$ preserve the levels (V7.6); the set $|X_\infty|$ and the identity $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$, immediate as $ml$ is constant on classes, are not stated (Findings, Chapter 7, items 6, 112).

notFormalized.title: The density of $X_\infty$ in $X_k$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ carry the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_k X_k$; the set $X_\infty$ is dense in every space $X_k$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the text states the density without proof; Part I proves it only for sc-Banach spaces (`ScBanach.denseRange_incl`), and its text does not state it for M-polyfolds or retracts. For a retract $O = r(U)$ it follows from the continuity of $r$ on level $k$ and the density of $U_\infty$ in $U_k$, which for $U$ open in a partial quadrant $C$ needs $C \cap E_\infty$ dense in $C \cap E_k$. Chapter 7 uses the filtration, never the density. Found by the round-trip audit (V7.6) (gap G.73; Findings, Chapter 7, item 116).
